articles.author: Elise Gregg
articles.description: The Black Mississippi teen's family questions whether his race contributed to his July 4th death on an island off the Mississippi coast.
articles.title: Questions remain after grand jury declines indictment in Nolan Wells' death

articles.author: Stephen Thompson
articles.description: Let's take a look at how and why "Choosin' Texas" has come to define and dominate the pop charts in 2026.
articles.title: 5 reasons why 'Choosin' Texas' is now the longest-running No. 1 hit of all time

articles.author: Chloe Veltman
articles.description: The allegations claim Braden Peters, also known as Clavicular, had non-consensual sex with the 17-year-old female victim after plying her with alcohol. Peters' representative denies the charges.
articles.title: Girl accuses Braden Peters, social media influencer known as 'Clavicular,' of rape

articles.author: Scott Neuman
articles.description: Days after President Trump barred reporters from three major news outlets from the White House, the administration has launched a 24/7 YouTube channel promising to put its "biggest moments all in one place."
articles.title: White House launches 'Trump TV' after ban on major news outlets

articles.author: Rachel Treisman
articles.description: The future of Trump's D.C. arch was already fraught. Then he rebranded it as a military complex. Experts say that only raises more legal and logistical questions.
articles.title: Trump's D.C. arch is now a military complex. Here's how that complicates things

articles.author: Meghan Collins Sullivan
articles.description: This year's shortlist is made up of former Booker winners and debut authors, with tales spanning a wide range of genres, from historical fiction to campus novel to dystopian fiction.
articles.title: The 2026 Booker Prize shortlist is 'writing at its best'

articles.author: Ari Daniel
articles.description: Scientists have found a species they've named the fire amoeba, which is capable of reproducing at 145°F and continuing to move up to temperatures of 147°F — a record for complex eukaryotic life.
articles.title: This 'fire amoeba' pushes the limit of what's possible for complex life

articles.author: Tom Huizenga
articles.description: As the classical concert season ramps up, two of America's finest orchestras will soon be led by new conductors when Daniel Harding takes over in Los Angeles and Elim Chan leads in San Francisco.
articles.title: Meet the future of the LA Philharmonic and San Francisco Symphony

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The Islamic State group-inspired attacks were among the deadliest in Sri Lanka's history, killing 42 foreigners.
articles.title: Sri Lanka court convicts 15 over deadly 2019 Easter bombings

articles.author: Aya Batrawy
articles.description: As the U.S. conflict with Iran drags, the Iranian-backed Houthis in Yemen have opened a new front, taking new territory and displacing more than 100,000 people.
articles.title: Houthis try to push deeper into western Yemen, upending life, witnesses tell NPR

articles.author: Ima Caldwell
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Andrew Bragg, the shadow housing minister, said he believes in “big debates” about housing after pushing his new proposal yesterday to allow people to use their superannuation as collateral to get a home loan.
The policy hasn’t been adopted by the opposition, and leader Angus Taylor said yesterday it wasn’t Coalition policy.
We’re a great country, and we should be able to have big debates, as we had in the 80s and 90s about national savings and housing and the like, which led, in fact, to the super guarantee. …
It’s very important that we look to calibrate the retirement and housing and superannuation systems to make sure that they’re getting the best outcomes for the Australian people.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: Albanese meets with Japan’s PM for first time since melon-gate; police offer $1m for Gus Lamont information

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
articles.description:
‘Radical’ report likely to influence party’s platform also proposes abolishing inheritance and capital gains taxes
A thinktank linked to Reform UK has called for the abolition of the state pension and £75bn worth of sweeping tax cuts in a “radical” report likely to influence the party’s platform for the next election.
The Centre for a Better Britain’s (CFABB) report – which also calls for weaker rules for UK banks and Trump-style investment accounts offering £1,000 to newborns – will be formally launched at a private event with City executives on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thinktank linked to Reform UK calls for abolition of state pension

articles.author: Penry Buckley
articles.description:
Sharangan Maheswaran says his bid for story on unsubstantiated rumour about then-Liberal minister David Elliott was ‘not a serious offer’

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A lawyer for fugitive property developer Jean Nassif offered a Liberal operative $1,000 if he could get media to write about an unsubstantiated extramarital affair and breach of Covid-19 restrictions by a New South Wales minister, the anti-corruption watchdog has heard.
Sharangan Maheswaran told the Independent Commission Against Corruption a message to lobbyist Jeremy Greenwood about placing a story about former Liberal minister David Elliott, was “not a serious offer”. He was shown a message to Greenwood in which he wrote he was “not joking”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Liberal operative was offered $1,000 to get media to cover ‘grubby rumour’ minister was having affair, Icac hears

articles.author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
articles.description:
Joyce would not say which Liberals he had spoken to, while Angus Taylor denied any conversations had taken place
Senior Liberals have rubbished claims by Barnaby Joyce that he has discussed One Nation offering the Coalition a pathway to minority government after the next election, accusing him of buyers remorse after defecting from the Nationals.
Joyce, who defected to join Pauline Hanson’s party in December, claimed on Tuesday night he had held talks with senior Liberals about a potential deal for supply and confidence to oust Anthony Albanese from power.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Senior Liberals rubbish Barnaby Joyce’s claim of talks over deal with One Nation as ‘figment of his imagination’

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Friend sobs in witness box and tells Sydney murder trial Baird was scared to go to the police

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Jesse Baird was “petrified” of Beau Lamarre-Condon because he was an armed police officer who could make a false allegation that would ruin his career, a court has heard.
Lamarre-Condon has been accused of fatally shooting Sydney couple Jesse Baird, 26, and Luke Davies, 29, with a police service weapon at Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jesse Baird ‘petrified’ of Beau Lamarre-Condon and kept repeating ‘he has a gun’, court hears

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell, Chris Hippensteel, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for US Breaking News emails

Trump is arriving at the UN HQ right now.
After very brief doorstep comments – almost exclusively mocking CNN - he answers a reporter’s very loud question by saying his message to Putin is: “settle the war.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump defends actions in Iran and Venezuela in UN General Assembly address amid rising tensions with allies – as it happened

articles.author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent
articles.description:
The move comes after Jamaica’s culture minister Olivia Grange travelled to the UK earlier this month to lodge the historic petition
King Charles has referred a landmark slavery reparations petition from Jamaica to a high-level UK appeals court for legal advice, Jamaica’s culture minister announced in parliament on Tuesday.
Referring to the move as a “really big deal”, Olivia Grange told Jamaica’s MPs the monarch had confirmed that their legal questions have been passed on to the London-based privy council – the final court of appeal for UK overseas territories and some Commonwealth countries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jamaica hails King’s decision to refer slavery reparations petition to privy council as ‘really big deal’

articles.author: Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
Flying from 2028, it is set to be the national carrier’s second ultra long-haul route after Sydney to London, due to take off in 2027

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Qantas says travellers will be able to fly between Sydney and New York in just 18 hours from mid-2028 when the airline launches its second ultra long-haul route, cutting at least three hours from the travel time.
The route will be the second in Qantas’ Project Sunrise expansion plans, with new Sydney to London direct flights planned for October 2027, after some delays.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Qantas announces 18-hour direct flights from Sydney to New York with onboard ‘wellbeing zones’

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Islamic State-inspired bombings of churches and hotels in 2019 was one of the country’s worst ever attacks
A court in Sri Lanka has convicted 15 men over their involvement in the 2019 Easter bombings that killed 267 people, and sentenced them each to at least 200 years in prison, meaning they will spend the rest of their lives behind bars.
Nearly 600 people were wounded in the suicide bomb attacks on 21 April that targeted three churches and three hotels across the country during Easter services and celebrations. The bombings, which were inspired by the Islamic State (IS) group, were among the deadliest attacks in Sri Lanka’s history.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sri Lanka Easter bombings: 15 sentenced to hundreds of years in prison each over deadly terror attacks

articles.author: Amelia Gentleman, Diane Taylor, Steven Morris and Ben Quinn
articles.description:
Thomas called followers to disrupt arrival of asylum seekers in Gosport, but Border Force instead transported them to Dover
Charities have condemned footage of far-right activist Daniel Thomas using a blade to slash an inflatable dinghy in the Channel while a rescue worker was onboard, in a further escalation of organised anti-immigration protest.
Hundreds of protesters gathered early on Tuesday evening at Gosport in Hampshire, aiming to disrupt the planned disembarkation of asylum seekers, but the Border Force vessels carrying them landed instead in Dover early on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Far-right activist Daniel Thomas slashes dinghy in Channel with blade while rescue worker onboard

articles.author: Patrick Butler and Will Parman
articles.description:
Wirral mother among renters turning to food banks as gap between a two-bed and housing benefit hits £158 a month – rising to as much as £324 in London
Do you prioritise paying the rent, putting food on the table or keeping the house warm in winter? In practice, says Laura Braddock, a single mum from Wirral, Merseyside, you always pay the rent first and improvise the rest. “If I’ve got a roof over our head, then everything else I can muddle through.”
The pressing problem for Braddock, 39, is that muddling through is getting harder. The monthly rent for her two-bedroom flat far outstrips the local housing allowance (LHA) she receives – and the gap may widen.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pay rent, eat or keep warm? Growing numbers face hard choices as housing benefit gap grows

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
IPPR North says one bad decision could derail devolution agenda as regions gain control of billions in funding
England’s mayors should face much greater official scrutiny to avoid Andy Burnham’s devolution agenda being “derailed by one bad decision”, a thinktank has said.
Ministers will set out plans next month to give regional leaders control over potentially billions of pounds of additional funding under a “transformational” shift of power outside Whitehall.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: England’s mayors should face greater scrutiny as powers expand, thinktank says

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
Surrogate who rejected abortion request had asked justices to halt court order recognizing LA couple as legal parents
The supreme court has refused to get involved with a custody dispute between an Alaska surrogate and a California couple whose child was born with a rare and serious heart defect.
On Tuesday, Justice Elena Kagan denied an emergency request from McKenna West, an Alaska nurse and surrogate who had asked the US’s highest court to halt a California court order recognizing the couple, Omar Ahmed and Nausheen Gilkar, as the boy’s legal parents.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US supreme court declines to intervene in custody fight over baby born via surrogate

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
County’s first such clinic, at Alder Hey in Liverpool, treating children suffering from chronic bladder problems with severe cases needing dialysis
Children as young as 13 in the UK have been referred to a specialist clinic for a “devastating” bladder condition linked to sustained use of ketamine.
Medics at Alder Hey children’s hospital in Liverpool opened the first ketamine clinic in the UK for young people amid a surge in urology problems linked to addiction of the drug.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Children as young as 13 being referred to UK hospital suffering from ‘ketamine bladder’

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
Former VP, who lost state to Trump in 2024 elections, is lending her popularity to unite fractured party
Kamala Harris returned to Michigan on Tuesday to campaign for Abdul El-Sayed, lending her popularity among Black voters to a progressive Senate nominee still working to unite a party fractured by a bruising primary – and the former vice-president’s loss to Donald Trump in the state.
Appearing with El-Sayed at a Detroit birth center, Harris used a roundtable on Black maternal health to frame that November’s contest against the Republican Mike Rogers as a fight over women’s access to care.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kamala Harris returns to Michigan to campaign for Abdul El-Sayed for Senate

articles.author: Timothy Pratt
articles.description:
Lawyers for James ‘Fergie’ Chambers, wanted over alleged support for Hamas, say client is being persecuted
The Spanish government has decided to allow the Trump administration’s controversial extradition request to extradite wealthy activist James “Fergie” Chambers to continue in the country’s courts.
Chambers, a US citizen and wealthy donor to leftwing and humanitarian projects, is currently imprisoned in Madrid. It is the first known case of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation tied to money Chambers has donated to support Palestinians, including the Sameer Project, in Gaza.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Spain allows US extradition case against pro-Palestine aid donor to proceed

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
US officials have begun to buy back wind leases as president seek to block renewables in favor of fossil fuels
Democratic attorneys general from California and New York have sued the Trump administration over its plans to buy back offshore wind leases as Donald Trump seeks to discourage the expansion of wind energy in favor of fossil fuels.
California attorney general Rob Bonta said he was suing over removal of a project off his state’s coast planned by Chicago-based Invenergy. The Trump administration said in June it was buying back the company’s US offshore wind leases for four wind projects on the east and west coasts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: California and New York sue over Trump push to halt wind energy projects

articles.author: Patrick Wintour in New York
articles.description:
Senior Iranian official indicates willingness to reopen strait of Hormuz if US takes steps to ease pressure on Tehran
Iranian officials held three hours of talks with US special envoy Steve Witkoff on the sidelines of the UN general assembly, Donald Trump disclosed on Tuesday.
He said there would a further meeting in the very near future.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran and US have held talks on sidelines of UN summit, says Donald Trump

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell
articles.description:
The park is the most highly visited and strong winds make trash problem worse, with gusts blowing away items
Hold on to your hats – Yellowstone national park staffers have removed a record-setting 20,100 pieces of trash from hydrothermal areas around the geyser-filled park so far this year
The most commonly found items include 280 hats, 54 camera lens caps, 47 hair ties, 42 pencils, 36 pairs of sunglasses, 20 hotel key cards and 17 baby pacifiers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hats, pencils and baby pacifiers: Yellowstone staffers retrieve record amount of trash from hot springs

articles.author: Lucy Campbell, Serena Richards, Tom Ambrose and Yohannes Lowe
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Tehran appears to have relaxed its preconditions for reopening the strait of Hormuz, saying it is prepared to do so within seven days so long as the US takes reciprocal steps to ease the pressure on Iran.
Previously Iran had set seven onerous pre-conditions for lifting the blockade including “an end to war on all fronts” and a commitment by the US to cease all aggressive actions against Iran including sanctions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Middle East crisis: Trump says Iran will make a deal after US midterms – as it happened

articles.author: Richard Luscombe
articles.description:
Polo, with sustained winds of 165mph, is churning 215 miles south of Zihuatanejo but is unlikely to directly hit Mexico
A tropical storm off the south-west coast of Mexico has intensified into a category 5 monster in fewer than 24 hours, fueled by stronger than usual El Niño weather patterns in the Pacific Ocean.
Hurricane Polo was sending out maximum sustained winds of 165mph (266km/h) on Tuesday as its center churned about 215 miles (346km) south of the coastal city of Zihuatanejo, in Guerrero state.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hurricane Polo, rapidly intensifying from strong El Niño patterns, rages off coast of Mexico

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
US president may have upstaged the ghost of Soviet leader Khrushchev by musing destruction of fellow member state
Donald Trump has a habit of discomfiting delegates to the United Nations general assembly. But this year, he may have upstaged the ghost of Nikita Khrushchev by openly contemplating the annihilation of a fellow UN member state.
Eleven minutes into a 40-minute address, the US president announced he had “a big decision to make” over Iran, which has staged a much more determined resistance than Trump anticipated when he decided to go to war against the country in February.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s threat to annihilate Iran to UN general assembly is stunning, even for him

articles.author: Agence France-Presse in Beijing
articles.description:
Lian Yunzhi solves 3x3 puzzle on several occasions in average time of under 4.5 seconds, according to state media
A six-year-old Chinese girl has set a new women’s world record for solving a Rubik’s Cube in just over four seconds, state media reported.
“Speedcuber” Lian Yunzhi broke the women’s 3x3 average world record twice this month at two World Cube Association certified competitions in Wuhan and Guangzhou, according to state broadcaster CCTV on Monday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Six-year-old Chinese girl ‘sets new women’s Rubik’s Cube world record’

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
articles.description:
Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman delisted in what Ireland’s EU presidency calls ‘a difficult compromise’ for the bloc
The EU has agreed to remove two Russian billionaires, Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, from its sanctions list, while extending restrictions on nearly 3,000 individuals and companies accused of supporting the war on Ukraine for the next three years.
With an end-of-Tuesday deadline looming to preserve the Russia blacklist, the EU’s 27 member states found a compromise that meant delisting the two oligarchs in spite of very few countries wanting this outcome. EU sanctions have to be approved unanimously.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU removes two oligarchs from Russia sanctions list as deadline looms

articles.author: Jakub Krupa (now and earlier) and Martin Belam (earlier)
articles.description:
Agreement signed at the UN general assembly in New York
Nordic correspondent 
Emotions among Greenlanders are a mixture of hope, scepticism and fear ahead of the signing of a new much vaunted deal on Arctic security between the US, Greenland and Denmark.
“There have been many different reactions in Greenland because they are talking about a deal but no one can see the deal, we don’t know what it is all about, and what’s in it for us or what’s in it. Also, because we have been terrorised as a people for the last 1.5 years by the American president, so many people feel no trust at all.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US to build new military bases in Greenland as deal seeks to end tensions between Nato allies - as it happened

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Officials say one pilot safely ejected as F-16 believed to have crashed on approach to Spangdahlem after training drill
⁠An F-16 fighter jet assigned to the US air ⁠base Spangdahlem ⁠in ​western Germany crashed on Tuesday, the US military said, ⁠adding that one pilot had ejected safely and was receiving ⁠medical treatment.
The cause of the incident ​is under ‌investigation, the military ‌said in a statement, with ‌emergency response personnel at the scene of the crash.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US fighter jet crashes at air base in western Germany

articles.author: Jess Cartner-Morley in Milan
articles.description:
Combination of Miuccia Prada with Belgian designer Raf Simons once again spins gold for fashion house
Miuccia Prada’s style formula is simple: begin with a great skirt. Her personal uniform is a knee-length skirt, A-line or pleated, most often with a plain sweater and kitten heels.
The Prada collection that opened Milan fashion week made a compelling case for her favourite outfit, with a skirt the star of every one of the 63 looks – no dresses, no trousers. It won the room over, so expect to see the personality skirt on a high street near you soon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Skirts given star billing as Prada swerves trousers and dresses in Milan

articles.author: William Christou in Beirut
articles.description:
Thousands flee fighting as Iran-aligned group seeks to consolidate territorial gains against Saudi-backed government forces

Middle East live – latest updates


As many as 169 people have been reportedly killed in Yemen in the last three days as Iran-aligned Houthis battle Saudi-backed government forces for control of strategic heights on the Red Sea coast, while thousands flee the violence.
Houthi military officials said at least 118 people had been killed in clashes as well as Saudi air and artillery strikes on Taiz, al-Jawf, Marib and Saada provinces since Sunday, Agence France-Presse reported. Yemeni government sources have said at least 36 people have been killed on their side of the conflict.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Up to 169 killed in Yemen as Houthis battle for Red Sea coastal heights

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
MPs send out letter as Israeli government seeks bids for construction of large E1 settlement in West Bank
British banks and financial institutions are receiving written warnings from MPs that they should not invest in Israel’s E1 settlement project even though new UK laws banning trade with illegal settlements are unlikely to be in place for months.
A letter was sent to banks on Tuesday by the all-party Britain-Palestine group of MPs saying the onus was now on banks to review their obligations not to cooperate with new settlements.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British banks warned not to invest in planned Israeli settlement before UK trade ban begins

articles.author: Sarah Basford Canales
articles.description:
Disappearance of jet components sparks concern some of the program’s technology secrets could have been exposed

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Department of Defence is examining how F-35 fighter jet parts bound for the US from Australia were unexpectedly diverted to Hong Kong, the acting prime minister, Richard Marles, has said.
Marles said “very much everything that has occurred at the Australian end” would be reviewed, but claimed the technology parts were not “sensitive”, as first reported by Politico over the weekend.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia investigating how F-35 fighter jet parts bound for US went missing in Hong Kong

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
Generations of artisans from Mumbai to Lucknow have shaped the world’s most coveted designs. Plus, the gen Z memes giving classic Bollywood a new life
The zardozi embroidery on a Dior dress, the T-strap leather sandals at a Prada show, the mirror-work technique used on a Fendi bag – for decades, the skill of Indian artisans has been an invisible force behind some of the world’s most coveted fashion.
Now, that work is beginning to claim its own place in the spotlight, and the Mumbai-based textile and embroidery atelier Chanakya International is at the forefront.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘What we have is unique’: the Indian craftsmanship behind global luxury fashion

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Rescuers search for missing in collapsed homes after storm causes landslides, travel chaos and power outages
Typhoon Dujuan has killed at least four people and injured 22 in Japan, while tens of thousands of houses near Tokyo remained without power after the storm swept through the region, authorities said on Tuesday.
Dujuan – which brought violent winds of 144km/h (89mph) – was moving away from Japan on Tuesday morning, allowing authorities to downgrade most heavy rain and landslide warnings.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At least four people killed in Japan as typhoon Dujuan triggers heavy rain, landslides

articles.author: Nick Robins-Early and agencies
articles.description:
Canadian province alleges deadly attack could have been prevented if  company had warned police of shooter’s ChatGPT use
British Columbia has sued OpenAI, saying a mass shooting at a school in the Canadian province could have been prevented if the company had warned local ⁠law enforcement that the shooter ⁠had used ChatGPT to ​plan the attack.
The lawsuit, filed in San Francisco federal court on Monday, names OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, as defendants. It is seeking damages to fund recovery efforts in the province after the February attack, as well as an order directing changes to the way the company handles ChatGPT conversations that could lead to violence.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British Columbia sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over Tumbler Ridge mass school shooting

articles.author: Tobi Thomas health and inequalities correspondent
articles.description:
Accra Reset’s report states countries in the region and global south should take greater control of their health development after USAID debacle
The United States’ withdrawal from key aid programs has put healthcare in Africa and the Global South “under growing strain” a new report warns.
The report says the Trump administration’s cuts to programs such as US Agency for International Development (USAID), as well as the Covid-19 pandemic and rising costs of living globally have brought “new urgency” for the need to reform healthcare in the region.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healthcare in Africa ‘under growing strain’ after US withdrawal from aid programs, report warns

articles.author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
articles.description:
Andy Burnham seeks stability in Middle East to bring down prices at home as first meeting with Trump looms
The UK has agreed to provide defensive air support to Saudi Arabia to help counter Houthi fighters and restore stability in the Middle East while driving down the cost of living at home, Andy Burnham has said, ahead of his first meeting with Donald Trump.
The prime minister said he had agreed to a request for air-to-air refuelling of Saudi jets to defend energy infrastructure against the Iran-backed rebels and help keep oil flowing from the Gulf to ease global economic turmoil.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK to give support to Saudi jets in attempt to counter Houthi fighters

articles.author: Associated Press in Bogotá
articles.description:
Wildfire forces evacuations and burns through mountains surrounding Villa de Leyva in the north-east 
Colombian authorities declared a public calamity as a wildfire burned through mountains surrounding one of the country’s best-known colonial towns in the north-east, scorching large swaths of vegetation and forcing evacuations.
Nearly 20 active fires are burning across the South American country. Dry conditions have increased fire danger in Colombia as it braces for the effects of El Niño, which can help wildfires spread.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Colombia declares public calamity as wildfire threatens popular tourist area

articles.author: Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad and Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Police crack down on family and political supporters of former PM who say authorities are ‘slowly killing’ him in prison
Three sisters of Pakistan’s incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan have been arrested amid a heavy-handed government crackdown on plans for a nationwide protest to demand Khan’s release.
The lawyer for the three sisters, Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, said on Monday that they had all been detained and jailed for 30 days under a warrant that accused them of being a threat to public order.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan jails sisters of Imran Khan before protest seeking his release

articles.author: Jodie Woodcock for MetDesk
articles.description:
Storm system expected to hit Izu Islands as it strengthens. Meanwhile, Atlantic hurricane season is unusually quiet
Tropical Storm Dujuan is skirting the coast of Japan and despite avoiding a direct landfall, is still expected to leave its mark. Dujuan briefly reached typhoon status on Friday before weakening to a tropical storm again on Sunday morning. But it is expected to restrengthen back to a typhoon by Tuesday morning. Sustained winds could reach 80mph (129km/h), with gusts approaching 100mph.
Although mainland Japan has avoided a direct hit, Dujuan’s track takes it across the Izu Islands, where evacuation warnings are in place. Heavy rain, flooding and landslide alerts are widespread, with high waves adding another threat to exposed coastal areas and islands.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Japanese islands brace for Dujuan to become a typhoon again

articles.author: Louisa Loveluck
articles.description:
After a plane journey in shackles, an Iranian woman found herself in the middle of Africa in a country she did not know existed. She is one of thousands deported from the US on the back of shadowy deals made with dozens of countries. An in-depth investigation reveals the ‘show of force’ costing American taxpayers millions
No one would tell the shackled detainees onboard the US immigration plane where they were going. The officers in charge would taunt them when they asked, they said. It was only when the seat-back video screens finally showed a map that the 18 migrants worked it out.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Banished to alien lands: Trump’s secret deportation deals

articles.author: Rebecca Bailey China correspondent
articles.description:
Beijing believes slowdown calls aim to lock in US advantage, and is pursuing a different balance between safety and pace

China bogeyman looms large over American firms’ AI doomsday scenario

About two years ago, education entrepreneur Boris But had what he calls a “penny-drop moment” – that, like countless others in China, his company needed to embrace AI before it was made obsolete by it.
His clients, well-off parents looking to send their children to study overseas, had begun arriving in his office reeling off information and opinions gleaned not from rival firms, but from chatbots.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why China is pushing back on US warnings over rapid AI development

articles.author: Maanvi Singh
articles.description:
Group trapped at Hotel Bamy after US removal as rights groups sound alarm over poor conditions and violence

Two men that the Trump administration expelled to Equatorial Guinea were bound, fitted with bags over their heads, beaten and pushed down a flight of stairs, all in plain view of other US deportees, according to witnesses and human rights lawyers.
The men – one from Egypt and one from Eritrea – were then taken to a prison. About 30 detainees from the US remain trapped at a hotel in the outskirts of the coastal city of Malabo after being deported from the US. Detainees have said they believe the men were beaten for telling the press and human rights advocates about the poor conditions and violence inside the hotel, and that they are haunted by flashbacks and terrified they will be retaliated against next.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Men deported from US bound and beaten in Equatorial Guinea detention hotel, lawyers say

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan and agencies
articles.description:
Police fire teargas as protests break out in city of Minna after deaths of suspected illegal goldminers, many of whom were children
Survivors from a prison cell in Nigeria where 37 suspected illegal goldminers died while in the custody of a paramilitary group this week have recounted their panic and struggle for breath, as police on Friday fired teargas at people protesting against the deaths and imposed an overnight curfew in the city of Minna.
The victims – many of whom were children – were found dead on Thursday in the cells of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), which had raided suspected illegal goldmines and ⁠locked up dozens of miners in the city, the state capital of the mineral-rich state of Niger.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Survivors recount panic and struggle to breathe in Nigerian prison cell where 37 died

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Jagtar Singh Johal, from Scotland, was arrested after wedding in Punjab on alleged terrorism offences
Jagtar Singh Johal, a British Sikh man who was arrested in India in 2017 in connection with alleged terrorism offences, has been granted bail by a Delhi court.
Johal, from Scotland, was arrested for his alleged role in funding the Khalistan Liberation Force, which had carried out targeted killings in India’s Punjab region.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British Sikh man granted bail in India nine years after arrest

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Four of Nusrat Osman’s alleged abductors were killed during rescue after she was taken from outside her home last week
A British woman kidnapped in Malawi last week has been rescued by police after a shootout in which four of her alleged abductors were killed.
Nusrat Osman was abducted outside her home in the southern city of Blantyre on 11 September at about 12.30pm. Police had offered a reward of 30m Malawi kwacha (£12,950) for information leading to her rescue and the arrest of the perpetrators.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British woman who was kidnapped in Malawi rescued by police after shootout

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Mohammad Sharifullah, 28, was convicted of aiding the terrorist group that took credit for the suicide bombing 
An Islamic State group member was sentenced on Wednesday to 20 years in prison for aiding the terrorist organization that took credit for a suicide bombing that killed 13 US service members and about 160 Afghans at the Kabul airport five years ago during the US military’s chaotic withdrawal from the country.
A federal jury in Virginia had convicted Mohammad Sharifullah in April of providing material support to the IS affiliate known as Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP). But jurors could not agree whether he bore some responsibility for the airport bombing on 26 August 2021.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: IS member sentenced to 20 years in prison for role in 2021 Kabul airport bombing

articles.author: Amy Hawkins, and David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Fears persist about Trump ‘sucking up’ to Xi on Taiwan, but few concrete outcomes anticipated from US meeting
When Xi Jinping, China’s leader, touches down in Maryland on Wednesday, he will step out into the arms – perhaps a hug, if Donald Trump’s wishes come true – of a US president who has shown China more bonhomie than any of his recent predecessors.
The meeting between Xi and Trump this week will be the second time that the leaders of the world’s two biggest economies have talked face to face this year. At the previous summit, held in Beijing in May, there was much talk of building a “strategic stability” between the two powers. But there was little by way of concrete outcomes: the countries remain at loggerheads over trade, export controls and geopolitics.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI looms large over Trump-Xi meeting amid deep distrust between US and China

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
US officials have begun to buy back wind leases as president seek to block renewables in favor of fossil fuels
Democratic attorneys general from California and New York have sued the Trump administration over its plans to buy back offshore wind leases as Donald Trump seeks to discourage the expansion of wind energy in favor of fossil fuels.
California attorney general Rob Bonta said he was suing over removal of a project off his state’s coast planned by Chicago-based Invenergy. The Trump administration said in June it was buying back the company’s US offshore wind leases for four wind projects on the east and west coasts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: California and New York sue over Trump push to halt wind energy projects

articles.author: Ted Widmer
articles.description:
Gone was any shred of US idealism. It was a spectacle of raw power – a power that is likely to only diminish in the years ahead
Expectations were low for Donald Trump’s address to the UN on Tuesday, and yet somehow it was even worse than expected. He does not perform well in formal settings, like chambers of government, preferring a blingier room, like Mar-a-Lago, or an outdoor rally. For years, he has made no secret of his hostility to the UN, and the very principles of international order that define it.
In recent years, that hostility has deepened into something more like a full-on assault, with frequent attacks on the international criminal court (perhaps out of fear that he will someday be indicted), on the UN’s climate agenda, and on Unesco (which the US decided to withdraw from in July 2025).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump invades the UN with a brutish speech | Ted Widmer

articles.author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
articles.description:
GOP nominee for governor Byron Donalds removes multiple mentions of president from his campaign website

US politics live – latest updates

Another prominent Florida Republican has publicly distanced himself from Donald Trump, days after María Elvira Salazar called out the US president’s immigration-enforcement policy targeting law-abiding undocumented immigrants.
Byron Donalds, the Republican nominee for governor in November’s US midterm elections, launched an updated campaign website on Tuesday that was stripped of almost every mention of Trump and removed a photograph of the congressman and his wife, Erika, posing with the president, the Miami Herald reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Another Florida Republican distances himself from Donald Trump before midterms

articles.author: Gaya Gupta
articles.description:
President made more than 440 purchases and 700 sales despite voter anger over elected officials trading stocks
Donald Trump made over a thousand stock sales and purchases worth between $79m and $270m in July, according to a Guardian analysis of his latest financial disclosure released Tuesday.
His two largest sales were of Amazon and Microsoft stock, selling between $5m and $25m each on 20 July. That same day, he also sold up to $5m worth of Oracle and Costco stock, $500,000 to $1m in Nvidia, and bought up to $5m worth of shares in Intuit and Salesforce, among dozens of other transactions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump made over 1,000 July stock trades worth up to $270m, filings reveal

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
But industry trade group says plan would backfire and lead to even higher prices for gasoline

US politics live – latest updates

Donald Trump on Tuesday said he backed ⁠the idea of a ban on diesel exports, which some US politicians are calling for ⁠as a way ⁠to curb ​the soaring cost of energy.
Diesel prices have rallied in Europe and the US to ⁠record highs as wars in Iran and Ukraine sharply cut exports from some of the biggest producers ⁠such as Russia, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. A gallon of diesel fuel in the US was $6.53 on Tuesday, the highest average on record and over 75% higher than a year ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says he backs diesel export ban to curb soaring energy costs

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Jake and Logan Paul were invited to give a motivational speech. Just don’t let them get involved with military policy
We’re now approaching month seven of a war against Iran that Donald Trump repeatedly assured us would be over in a matter of weeks. Prices are rising, troop morale is plummeting, and there is little evidence things will improve.
The situation is so desperate that the decision makers at the Pentagon have decided to bring out the big guns. I’m not talking about nuclear weapons, although Trump recently threatened to “blow the entire nation [of Iran] up”. No, I’m talking about influencers Jake and Logan Paul, who are famous for doing idiotic stunts on YouTube and getting hit in the face during boxing matches. Last Thursday, Pete Hegseth’s Department of Defense or whatever they’re calling it these days (the Department of War Crimes?) welcomed the Paul brothers to Washington DC “to meet with our warriors” and deliver a motivational speech. In response, former Republican congressman and air force officer Adam Kinzinger wrote, “We aren’t a serious country at the moment.” That about sums it up.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Pentagon has unveiled its secret weapon: two idiotic influencers | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Leslie Vinjamuri
articles.description:
Mark Rutte has the right idea – go beyond Washington and make the case for the transatlantic alliance to the public. They may well have a willing ear
At a moment when Europe is focused on persuading Donald Trump to remain committed to Nato, it needs to convince Americans, too. So the presence this evening of the Nato secretary general, Mark Rutte, in front of a public audience in Des Moines, Iowa, is significant. This is the home town of Trump’s ambassador to Nato, Matthew Whitaker, and the visit brings the debate over Nato’s future directly to a midwestern audience in a red state that operates far from elite foreign-policy circles in Washington. Rutte’s appearance is long overdue.
Russia’s war in Ukraine and uncertainty over the US commitment to European security have forced European leaders to confront their dependence on Washington. While some are pressing for building European capabilities as a means to separate from the US, others see greater European defence spending as essential to keeping the US engaged. Either way, European governments can’t rely solely on meetings with Trump to secure the alliance’s future.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Never mind Trump – if Europe wants to save Nato, it must win over the American people | Leslie Vinjamuri

articles.author: Martin Belam
articles.description:
White House press coverage row continues while anchor-less channel of the administration’s ‘latest and greatest’ streams propaganda for the Maga faithful
Donald Trump’s previous television career centred on his role on The Apprentice, but the US president’s latest media venture is a rather lower-budget affair: the launch of Trump TV in the wake of his ban on several outlets from covering the White House.
With major US networks agreeing to not cover the president while the dispute continues, on Monday the White House announced the new 24/7 YouTube live stream, which it promised would feature “top past moments, announcements, and the latest and greatest from the administration all in one place”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Literally state-run TV’: Trump launches YouTube channel amid boycott by US networks

articles.author: Stephanie Kirchgaessner
articles.description:
Carr was a member of the group in his teens and 20s. There is no evidence Trump’s powerful FCC chair participated in any inappropriate conduct
Brendan Carr, the chair of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), was for about a decade a member of a rogue Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) group when he was in his late teens and 20s that some former members compared to a “cult”, according to a Guardian investigation.
The Midtown group, which was based in the Washington DC area, attracted young people who were seeking help with addiction, sometimes at the urging of their parents.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brendan Carr was a member of a rogue Alcoholics Anonymous group some labeled a ‘cult’

articles.author: Stephen Starr in Detroit
articles.description:
The Democratic Senate nominee’s views on Israel and comments after a synagogue attack prompted a public debate among Jewish voters
When Jess Newman heard that Temple Israel in Detroit was attacked last March, her first thoughts went to her extended family.
“I grew up going to services there,” she said. “The attack was awful. My Jewish identity is very important to me.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed’s candidacy has split the Jewish community

articles.author: Robert Reich
articles.description:
It’s becoming obvious to many Americans that corporations have been raking it in while workers take it on the chin
Last week, the unlikely duo of Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon spoke before a Washington group demanding a stop to AI and its datacenters.
Notably, both lambasted the corporate oligarchs behind AI.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI is generating a new wave of US populism. It could be a tipping point | Robert Reich

articles.author: Akbar Shahid Ahmed
articles.description:
Voters rejected many establishment choices this year in favor of candidates pushing accountability for Gaza, writes Akbar Shahid Ahmed
The last time she gathered with fellow Democrats for a pre-election national convention, Georgia state representative Ruwa Romman got an unspoken message from the party establishment: on their biggest stage, she said, “There’s room for an anti-choice Republican but not for Palestinians”. Democratic officials gave speaking slots to an architect of Georgia’s strict abortion ban and other conservatives critical of Donald Trump, but they denied a speech from Romman or other Palestinian Americans.
In Democratic primaries this year, voters rejected many of the party establishment’s choices, including a 15-term congresswoman in Colorado and the chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus. The unlikely winners in all those races emphasized empathy and accountability for Palestinian losses in Gaza; Abdul El-Sayed, who won Michigan’s Senate primary, made opposition to the ardently pro-Israel group Aipac central to his candidacy. With 60% of potential Democratic voters in a May poll sympathizing more with Palestinians than Israelis and 48% saying the party has been too supportive of Israel, the base is eager for Democratic leaders to rethink unfettered US-Israel solidarity.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrats’ Gaza reckoning: how failing to give Palestinians a voice came back to bite the party

articles.description:
Protesters in Austin, Texas, demonstrated against the Trump administration’s hardline anti-immigration campaign after an ICE agent shot and wounded a man on Sunday afternoon. Eyewitness footage filmed moments after the shooting shows the ICE officer standing next to an open car door, in which there is a visible dent. The man, identified by relatives and his lawyer as 28-year-old Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, was taken to a hospital in Austin in a serious but stable condition, officials said, before being taken into custody.
The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, said it was leading an investigation into the officer involved in the shooting, with the help of the FBI. Austin police officers were not involved in the operation or the shooting, which occurred after a traffic stop, mayor Kirk Watson stated at a press conference 

ICE agent shoots and wounds Venezuelan man at traffic stop in Austin, Texas

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Protesters gather in Austin after ICE agent shoots and wounds man – video

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland with Blake Montgomery , produced by Nada Smiljanic and John Rogers; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
Tech bosses have called for a slowdown in artificial intelligence and formal guardrails to be introduced by the US government. But President Trump is not moved by the doomsday predictions, calling them a ‘hoax'. What is behind his affection for the AI industry? Jonathan Freedland and Guardian US tech editor Blake Montgomery discuss
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is Trump’s AI obsession walking the world into disaster? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman with Johana Bhuiyan . Produced by Tiara Chiaramonte engineered by Ivan Kuraev executive producers Jonathan Menjivar and Rachel Humphreys
articles.description:
A former Anthropic researcher’s apocalyptic declaration about artificial intelligence has led to a global panic that the technology might be the end of us all. At an event in Washington today to warn about the dangers of AI, US senator Bernie Sanders said that Congress has been ‘asleep at the wheel'. Oddly, Steve Bannon appeared at the same event. But is this response a distraction from the more immediate problems AI is already causing? Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by Guardian tech reporter Johana Bhuyian to put this moment in context, and she explains why we should be cynical about industry calls for regulation
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why the real AI apocalypse is already here – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.description:
During a Senate committee hearing, FBI director answered questions from Republican senator John Kennedy about the bureau's new policy allowing the hiring of people who have engaged in bestiality
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kash Patel defends changes in FBI hiring policy regarding bestiality – video

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
articles.description:
‘Radical’ report likely to influence party’s platform also proposes abolishing inheritance and capital gains taxes
A thinktank linked to Reform UK has called for the abolition of the state pension and £75bn worth of sweeping tax cuts in a “radical” report likely to influence the party’s platform for the next election.
The Centre for a Better Britain’s (CFABB) report – which also calls for weaker rules for UK banks and Trump-style investment accounts offering £1,000 to newborns – will be formally launched at a private event with City executives on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thinktank linked to Reform UK calls for abolition of state pension

articles.author: Written by Melissa Denes and read by Ruth Lass. Originally produced and sound designed by Jessica Beck with additions from Nicola Alexandrou. The executive producer was Ellie Bury
articles.description:
We are raiding the Guardian long read archives to bring you some classic pieces from years past, with new introductions from the authors.
This week, from 2023: For the past two years, Betsy Stanko has been leading an unprecedented investigation into why the police have been failing so badly to tackle sexual violence. But is there any chance of fixing a system that seems so broken?
By Melissa Denes. Read by Ruth Lass
Read the text version here
Support the Guardian today: theguardian.com/longreadpod
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From the archive: ‘I know where the bodies are buried’: one woman’s mission to change how the police investigate rape – podcast

articles.author: Amelia Gentleman, Diane Taylor, Steven Morris and Ben Quinn
articles.description:
Thomas called followers to disrupt arrival of asylum seekers in Gosport, but Border Force instead transported them to Dover
Charities have condemned footage of far-right activist Daniel Thomas using a blade to slash an inflatable dinghy in the Channel while a rescue worker was onboard, in a further escalation of organised anti-immigration protest.
Hundreds of protesters gathered early on Tuesday evening at Gosport in Hampshire, aiming to disrupt the planned disembarkation of asylum seekers, but the Border Force vessels carrying them landed instead in Dover early on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Far-right activist Daniel Thomas slashes dinghy in Channel with blade while rescue worker onboard

articles.author: Patrick Butler and Will Parman
articles.description:
Wirral mother among renters turning to food banks as gap between a two-bed and housing benefit hits £158 a month – rising to as much as £324 in London
Do you prioritise paying the rent, putting food on the table or keeping the house warm in winter? In practice, says Laura Braddock, a single mum from Wirral, Merseyside, you always pay the rent first and improvise the rest. “If I’ve got a roof over our head, then everything else I can muddle through.”
The pressing problem for Braddock, 39, is that muddling through is getting harder. The monthly rent for her two-bedroom flat far outstrips the local housing allowance (LHA) she receives – and the gap may widen.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pay rent, eat or keep warm? Growing numbers face hard choices as housing benefit gap grows

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
IPPR North says one bad decision could derail devolution agenda as regions gain control of billions in funding
England’s mayors should face much greater official scrutiny to avoid Andy Burnham’s devolution agenda being “derailed by one bad decision”, a thinktank has said.
Ministers will set out plans next month to give regional leaders control over potentially billions of pounds of additional funding under a “transformational” shift of power outside Whitehall.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: England’s mayors should face greater scrutiny as powers expand, thinktank says

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
County’s first such clinic, at Alder Hey in Liverpool, treating children suffering from chronic bladder problems with severe cases needing dialysis
Children as young as 13 in the UK have been referred to a specialist clinic for a “devastating” bladder condition linked to sustained use of ketamine.
Medics at Alder Hey children’s hospital in Liverpool opened the first ketamine clinic in the UK for young people amid a surge in urology problems linked to addiction of the drug.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Children as young as 13 being referred to UK hospital suffering from ‘ketamine bladder’

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
Test using urine and vaginal fluid samples raises hopes thousands of lower-risk women could be spared internal ultrasounds and hysteroscopies
Doctors have developed a simple test that could help rule out womb cancer in women who experience bleeding after menopause.
The approach has the potential to transform care for thousands of women each year and spare them from invasive and uncomfortable tests that can also be costly for healthcare systems.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK doctors develop non-invasive test for womb cancer in women bleeding after menopause

articles.author: Pippa Crerar in New York and Kiran Stacey in London
articles.description:
US president calls UK prime minister ‘a natural businessperson’ as leaders meet at UN assembly in New York
Donald Trump has asserted his relationship with the UK is “more up” with Andy Burnham than under Keir Starmer despite tensions between the two countries on a range of thorny issues including regulation of artificial intelligence, the Chagos islands and the war in Iran.
At their first face-to-face meeting, the US president praised Burnham, who sat nervously alongside him, as a “natural businessperson”, saying he thought he had “lots of assets on his side” and would be a “great” prime minister.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump praises relations with Burnham despite tensions over AI and Iran

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
US president says Burnham will be ‘a great PM’ in friendly first meeting on the sidelines of UN General Assembly but makes jibe at Starmer
If Andy Burnham wanted to inject some edge into his meeting with Donald Trump later (which he doesn’t), he could bring along a copy of today’s Financial Times. This front page headline speaks for itself.
Mortgages ‘on the front line’ as Iran war deals £840 blow to homeowners
British homeowners are paying an average of £840 a year more when they refinance their mortgages, as the rising borrowing costs triggered by the Iran war start to impact consumers’ spending power.
Approximately 1m households have rolled off fixed-rate mortgage deals since February, according to Bank of England data.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK politics: Trump says he has a better UK relationship with Burnham as PM – as it happened

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
US president says British PM has a ‘lot of assets on his side’ as pair meet at UN in New York

Donald Trump has praised Andy Burnham as a “natural businessperson” and said the UK was “more up” than under Keir Starmer. But he berated the UK for its decision to give up the Chagos Islands.
In their first face-to-face meeting, Trump gave a warm assessment of the relationship, saying he thought Burnham had a “lot of assets on his side” and would be a “great prime minister”, adding: “We talked about everything from Rolls-Royce to energy to immigration – we covered a lot.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Donald Trump praises ‘natural businessperson’ Andy Burnham after first meeting

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
Entire £233m budget for 2026 allocated in less than a day, leaving thousands of farmers disappointed
Thousands of farmers have been left empty-handed with the government’s 2026 nature funding spent in just six hours.
The £233m sustainable farming incentive (SFI) scheme opened for applications from farmers at 10am on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Worse than the scramble for Oasis tickets’: England’s sustainable farming funds run out in just six hours

articles.author: Josh Halliday and Robyn Vinter
articles.description:
Charity’s head coach ‘shocked’ after Sunderland council leader says it will not support ‘politically charged’ groups
Anti-racism education in some schools will be scrapped after a city council now led by Reform UK ended its 30-year support for the charity Show Racism the Red Card.
Announcing the decision last week, the Reform leader of Sunderland city council, Christopher Eynon, said it would no longer support “politically charged organisations with an agenda”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reform UK-led council ends support for Show Racism the Red Card

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
articles.description:
Billionaire owner of Ineos says company ‘cannot compete’ with global market despite efficiency of Humberside sites
Billionaire industrialist Sir Jim Ratcliffe is pausing production at three chemical plants in Hull, blaming the UK’s “ridiculously high” gas prices.
Ratcliffe’s chemicals conglomerate, Ineos, said on Tuesday it would “mothball” three chemical plants because the cost made it difficult to compete in the global market.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jim Ratcliffe halts production at Hull chemical plants over ‘ridiculous’ gas prices

articles.author: Jamie Grierson and Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Brother of Diana, Princess of Wales, says ‘accuracy is important’ as he responds to broadcaster’s threat to sue over claims made in memoir
Earl Spencer has apologised to Piers Morgan for incorrectly claiming in his new book about Diana, Princess of Wales, that the former tabloid editor was behind the publication of intrusive photos of the late royal in the mid-1990s.
Morgan had earlier threatened to sue Spencer over “fabricated inaccuracies” and “examples of brazen falsity” in the book, which was published on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Earl Spencer apologises to Piers Morgan over ‘incorrect assumption’

articles.author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
articles.description:
The former UK deputy prime minister is a board member of the UK-based  company and owns 917,000 shares
Nick Clegg could make approximately $40m (£30m) from the planned float of Nscale as the UK-based datacentre company prepares for a US stock market listing.
The former UK deputy prime minister owns more than 917,000 shares in the startup, which is reportedly seeking a valuation of up to $35bn in a flotation. Based on Clegg’s stake of 0.12%, that could yield a valuation of about $42m for the ex-Liberal Democrat party leader.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nick Clegg could make £30m windfall from datacentre startup Nscale flotation

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Forestry England invites people to help it create a record of when and how the season arrives across the country
The reds and golds of autumn leaves may be beginning to appear, but exactly when the season arrives is not always as predictable as the calendar might suggest.
Now, Forestry England is asking people to help track the changing colours of forests to create a record of when and how autumn arrives across the country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Could you be an ‘autumn spotter’? Public asked to track changing colours of trees in England

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Some economists say it is now ‘inevitable’ that chancellor will need to raise taxes in the budget next month
The UK government borrowed a higher-than-expected £18.3bn last month, increasing the pressure on John Healey as he attempts to calm jittery bond markets before next month’s budget.
Some economists said it was “inevitable” that the chancellor would need to raise taxes on 28 October if he is to meet demands for extra spending on defence without further borrowing from investors on international money markets.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK borrows £18bn in August, putting pressure on Healey before budget

articles.author: Peter Walker and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
Growth created by rejoining EU single market and customs union would fund change, Davey tells the party’s conference

UK politics live – latest updates

Ed Davey has unveiled a plan for a £17bn income tax cut in a speech aimed at shoring up the party’s support among former Conservative voters, but which risked disappointing some Liberal Democrat MPs who want a bolder vision for the party.
Addressing the party’s annual conference in Brighton, the Lib Dem leader said the proposal, which would eventually increase the threshold for paying income tax to £15,000 and raise the level at which people pay the 40p higher rate by about £6,000, would be paid for entirely by increased growth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ed Davey promises £17bn income tax cut if Lib Dems are elected

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
MPs send out letter as Israeli government seeks bids for construction of large E1 settlement in West Bank
British banks and financial institutions are receiving written warnings from MPs that they should not invest in Israel’s E1 settlement project even though new UK laws banning trade with illegal settlements are unlikely to be in place for months.
A letter was sent to banks on Tuesday by the all-party Britain-Palestine group of MPs saying the onus was now on banks to review their obligations not to cooperate with new settlements.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British banks warned not to invest in planned Israeli settlement before UK trade ban begins

articles.author: Zoe Wood
articles.description:
EVs with 90,000 to 120,000 miles on the clock are more likely to pass MOTs than petrol models of the same age
Motorists buying a secondhand car with a lot of miles on the clock are likely to find an electric vehicle (EV) ultimately more reliable than a petrol vehicle, according to a study.
An analysis of 47.4m MOT tests found that after cars were driven 90,000 to 120,000 miles, EVs were about 25% less likely to fail than petrol models of the same age (based on a failure rate of 16.5% versus 22.1%).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: High-mileage electric cars are more reliable than petrol ones, study finds

articles.author: Donna Ferguson
articles.description:
The Argiope bruennichi, spotted in Cheshire for first time, part of worrying trend that could threaten native species
She is an unlikely harbinger of the climate emergency: a venomous black and yellow spider who spins mysterious patterns in her webs and eats her mates for breakfast.
Native to mainland Europe, north Africa and Asia, the Argiope bruennichi – commonly known as a wasp spider – is rarely seen in the north and west of Britain. But a fully grown female has been spotted in Cheshire for the first time by conservationists from Chester zoo, who stumbled across the large, brightly striped arachnid in a rewilded field.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Wasp spider seen in north of England latest ‘climate refugee’ amid global heating

articles.author: Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Broadcaster refutes memoir claim that he was behind publication of gym photos of Diana, Princess of Wales
Piers Morgan has said he will sue Earl Spencer over “fabricated inaccuracies” and “examples of brazen falsity” in his book about Diana, Princess of Wales.
The earl has made a series of claims in Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, including that King Charles said “we’ll forget her soon enough” after she died, which has prompted a war of words between him and Buckingham Palace.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Piers Morgan says he will sue Earl Spencer over ‘fabricated inaccuracies’

articles.author: David Renshaw
articles.description:
The country’s licensing laws mean the supermarket has opened a pub so it can sell alcohol, while campaigners are fighting to help other venues open and get people dancing
At first sight The Middle Ale in Dundonald, Northern Ireland looks just like any other pub. There is a big TV, an array of seating, and beer pumps behind the bar. Look a little closer, however, and you might ask why there are packets of fajitas and gravy granules on the walls.
That’s because the pub belongs to the supermarket chain Lidl, but the Middle Ale (like “middle aisle”, get it?) isn’t just a wacky marketing stunt. Northern Ireland has ultra-strict laws around licences to sell alcohol, whether as a shop, pub or nightclub. Lidl tried to get a licence to sell alcohol in its Dundonald store, and was refused, but after a court battle it did manage to get a licence for a pub – which it duly opened next door, selling alcohol to take away as well as serving drinks in the pub itself.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fancy a pint … at Lidl? The bizarre battle over Northern Ireland’s stifled nightlife

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Party strategists say careful targeting of seats has paid off and should continue, but some say a wider vision is needed
One of the more dramatic moments in a Liberal Democrat conference otherwise short of them came late on Sunday, when the party frontbencher Lisa Smart told the polling veteran John Curtice that, in effect, he no longer understood modern politics.
Curtice had warned the Lib Dems they risked being left behind, with the lack of a coherent national message seeing them all but ignored outside a few electoral strongholds. Smart’s response? In the new era of five- or six-party politics, and mass tactical voting, this does not matter.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lib Dems torn over whether to be voters’ first choice or the route to block Reform

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
Changes could save £33bn and result in average of four extra years of good health for people, report says
The NHS in England could prevent 20,000 deaths and save £33bn a year by cutting red tape and boosting productivity, a report says.
Research by the Health Foundation found the health service has been held back for decades by excessive regulation, short-term planning and insufficient capability to deliver major change.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cut NHS red tape and boost productivity to prevent 20,000 early deaths a year in England, report urges

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
Nats says fault at Prestwick has been ‘fixed’ after airports in Scotland, northern England and Northern Ireland are hit
Airlines have called for “action and accountability” over the UK’s air traffic control services after a technical issue led to flights being disrupted for the second time in a fortnight.
Dozens were cancelled and others severely delayed after a fault on Monday morning at National Air Traffic Services (Nats), this time at its second control centre at Prestwick in South Ayrshire.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Airlines urge action after UK flights delayed and cancelled again

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
The number of potentially damaging environmental incidents triggered by this year’s hot and dry weather has surpassed that of 2025
Wildlife in England and Wales will be affected by the current drought for years to come, the government has said.
This summer saw large parts of England and all of Wales plunged into a serious drought, with both recording their driest Julys since records began in 1836.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Wildlife will be affected by current drought for years to come, UK government says

articles.author: Presented by Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey, produced by John Rogers and Nada Smiljanic, music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
The UK prime minister will meet the US president for the first time in New York on Tuesday. With Trump at his weakest in the polls, could this be a perfect moment for Burnham to charm the president and avoid a very public political spat? Pippa and Kiran discuss what the two leaders might discuss in policy terms, and some of the potential high-risk issues
Please keep sending your comments and questions to Pippa and Kiran on politicsweeklyuk@theguardian.com
Watch this episode and subscribe to our YouTube channel here

articles.title: Can Andy Burnham pull off the ‘Mamdani effect’ on Donald Trump? – podcast

articles.author: Rachel Hall
articles.description:
Claimants having to find decades-old medical records to prove they qualify for compensation despite inquiry’s recommendations
Suzanne Morgan will never forget the day her mother died. It was nine months after she had gone into hospital with gallstones, where she received a routine blood transfusion.
“She went downhill rapidly,” Morgan recalled. Her mother haemorrhaged in her liver, and the next day she was dead.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I have to keep reliving it’: infected blood claimants being asked to prove eligibility

articles.author: Matthew Ponsford
articles.description:
Exclusive: The tax-funded brainchild of Dominic Cummings hopes to find ways to speed up wild species’ evolution
Vaccines for ash trees, skin treatments for newts and gene-edited swallowtail butterflies are among 14 tax-funded projects from the UK’s “invention agency” aiming to accelerate nature’s ability to adapt to the climate crisis.
The £54m accelerated adaptation programme from the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency (Aria) – a public body that funds high-risk, high-reward tech projects – aims to investigate applications of biotechnology that can speed up wild species’ evolution and help them to adapt to new threats such as global warming and disease.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tree vaccines and gene-edited butterflies among biotechnology projects funded by UK ‘invention agency’

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff in Jersey
articles.description:
While global billionaires and multinational companies have been lured to its shores, many islanders feel left behind and priced out, with food bank use increasing
On a late Friday afternoon on the Channel Island of Jersey, tourists and locals are flocking to St Helier’s waterfront where the town’s sprawling beach has emerged at low tide.
In one direction, they face the calm waters of St Aubin’s Bay, ringed by a seaside promenade and punctuated with a tidal island hosting the 16th century Elizabeth Castle.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s unrecognisable’: How being a tax haven has changed Jersey

articles.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Peter Walker; produced by Saskia Collette and Brian McNamara; executive producer Sami Kent
articles.description:
From hospital wards to bathrooms, where is a transgender person supposed to go after the latest equalities guidance?
Transgender people in Britain are navigating a new reality. In August, new guidance – in the form of a document nearly 350 pages long – was published to help institutions interpret last year’s supreme court ruling on trans rights.
It means, as Amelia outlines to Helen Pidd, that every time she goes to a pub or restaurant, she is terrified about going to the bathroom. As a trans woman, she has used women’s facilities without problems for years; now she’s being told she should use the men’s.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Being trans in Britain in 2026 – podcast

articles.author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
articles.description:
PM hopes to be firmer with US leader than his predecessor without provoking diplomatic warfare, as the Iran war weighs on the UK economy
No international relationship has more power to determine the success of Andy Burnham’s premiership. So you might imagine the stakes for the prime minister’s first face-to-face meeting with Donald Trump on Tuesday would be high.
Yet Burnham may prove to be a lucky general. The balance of risk has shifted. Trump is unpopular at home, where inflation remains high, and is mired in an intractable conflict in Iran that has the potential to sink his midterm dreams.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham faces a weakened Trump – but the president remains unpredictable

articles.author: Anna Bawden Health and social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Charity says NHS data shows increased chances of death due to preventable physical illnesses
An analysis of NHS data has shed light on the “scandal” of why adults with severe mental illness are more likely to die 15 to 20 years younger than the general population.
The Rethink Mental Illness charity has revealed that adults under 75 with serious mental ill health – defined as those referred to specialist secondary mental health services – are 6.3 times as likely to die from liver disease, 6 times more likely from respiratory illness, 3.8 times more likely from cardiovascular disease and 2.3 times as likely from cancer.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Early deaths are not inevitable’: report reveals why adults with severe mental illness die younger

articles.author: Alex Lawson
articles.description:
Unit1 hopes to offer lower cost version of shows such as Abba Voyage, showcasing living and dead artists in any venue
The former chief executive of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s entertainment group has obtained a near-£15m investment for his UK music tech startup that hopes to recreate classic concerts by manifesting musicians as digital avatars.
Unit1 was set up last year by Barney Wragg, an entertainment executive who ran Lord Lloyd-Webber’s Cats-to-Evita empire for five years from late 2011. It has secured the $20m in funding from a group of investors, including tech backer Balderton Capital through its partner Daniel Waterhouse, who made early investments in Spotify.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK startup snares $20m to recreate gigs with ‘hyper-realistic’ digital avatars

articles.description:
Cole, described as an ‘extraordinary talent’, also appeared in Waiting for God, Tenko and had an extensive theatre career

Stephanie Cole – a life in pictures

Stephanie Cole – obituary


The actor Stephanie Cole, best known for roles in Coronation Street, Waiting for God and Open All Hours, has died aged 84.
She also appeared in the prisoner-of-war drama Tenko, A Bit of a Do and Doc Martin.

Buckingham Palace has issued a rare, and strong, rebuttal to claims made in Earl Spencer’s memoir Swan Song. The book claims that King Charles told Spencer days after Diana’s death and during a heated row over funeral arrangements: ‘Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough.’ Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s senior national news editor, Aaron Sharp
